text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers refactor to make programs easier to read and understand. For example, they might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. The main goal is to keep the same behavior while making the code cleaner. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor designs are left in place. Although refactoring takes time, it saves effort later because clean code is easier to maintain, test, and update.
